lessons.key: ac_gap::when an acceptance criterion lists multiple failure sub cases for one field e g not parseable vs parseable but missing x write a distinct test per sub case rather than one representative test per field
lessons.text: When an acceptance criterion lists multiple failure sub-cases for one field (e.g. not-parseable vs. parseable-but-missing-X), write a distinct test per sub-case rather than one representative test per field.

lessons.key: spec_precision_gap::before writing an acceptance criterion that names two distinct failure triggers e g broker unreachable vs delivery timeout confirm the planned implementation actually has two distinct code paths for them or phrase it as one ac to avoid an unfalsifiable precision gap at validation time
lessons.text: Before writing an acceptance criterion that names two distinct failure triggers (e.g. broker-unreachable vs. delivery-timeout), confirm the planned implementation actually has two distinct code paths for them, or phrase it as one AC to avoid an unfalsifiable precision gap at validation time.
evidence: spec.md P1 'Publish failure is never silently accepted' AC4 (spec-writing)

lessons.key: spec_precision_gap::a spec acceptance criterion claiming a memory or performance property should also state the observable proxy to test it by or validation can only prove it by code inspection rather than by assertion
lessons.text: A spec acceptance criterion claiming a memory or performance property should also state the observable proxy to test it by, or validation can only prove it by code inspection rather than by assertion.

lessons.key: spec_deviation::testcontainers kafkacontainer with kraft enforces confluent platform s own version numbering and rejects tags below 7 0 0 so it cannot be pinned to a non confluent broker image e g apache kafka regardless of that image s real kafka version verify testcontainers image compatibility empirically before assuming a project s real broker image can be reused in an integration test
lessons.text: testcontainers' KafkaContainer.with_kraft() enforces Confluent Platform's own version numbering and rejects tags below 7.0.0, so it cannot be pinned to a non-Confluent broker image (e.g. apache/kafka) regardless of that image's real Kafka version -- verify testcontainers image compatibility empirically before assuming a project's real broker image can be reused in an integration test.

lessons.key: ac_gap::when an acceptance criterion requires a log record to carry a specific identifier assert that identifier is present not only that forbidden content is absent
lessons.text: When an acceptance criterion requires a log record to carry a specific identifier, assert that identifier is present, not only that forbidden content is absent.

lessons.text: When the design deliberately inverts an acceptance criterion, amend that criterion in the spec in the same change, or spec and code disagree in writing at validation time.

lessons.key: surviving_mutant::process lifecycle wiring such as signal handlers and startup hooks needs a test asserting it was armed because no functional test exercises it
lessons.text: Process-lifecycle wiring such as signal handlers and startup hooks needs a test asserting it was armed, because no functional test exercises it.

lessons.key: surviving_mutant::test both sides of every numeric threshold an acceptance criterion names the last passing value and the first failing one or an off by one in the comparison survives
lessons.text: Test both sides of every numeric threshold an acceptance criterion names, the last passing value and the first failing one, or an off-by-one in the comparison survives.

lessons.key: surviving_mutant::an integration test claiming a configuration value is load bearing must be shown to fail when that value is reverted to its default or it proves only that the scenario works
lessons.text: An integration test claiming a configuration value is load-bearing must be shown to fail when that value is reverted to its default, or it proves only that the scenario works.

lessons.key: spec_precision_gap::an acceptance criterion phrased as a negative universal such as no behaviour shall depend on x gives no test to write so restate it as a concrete observation that can be asserted
lessons.text: An acceptance criterion phrased as a negative universal such as no behaviour shall depend on X gives no test to write, so restate it as a concrete observation that can be asserted.

lessons.key: surviving_mutant::when a use case wraps multiple writes in one db transaction for atomicity add a test that injects a failure between the writes and asserts both are rolled back happy path and reject all writes tests alone don t prove the transaction boundary does anything
lessons.text: When a use case wraps multiple writes in one DB transaction for atomicity, add a test that injects a failure between the writes and asserts both are rolled back — happy-path and reject-all-writes tests alone don't prove the transaction boundary does anything

lessons.key: spec_precision_gap::when a spec ac s then clause has multiple parts status code error message content no db change assert every part not just the status code a passing status code assertion can hide an unenforced message or db state clause
lessons.text: When a spec AC's THEN clause has multiple parts (status code, error message content, no DB change), assert every part, not just the status code — a passing status-code assertion can hide an unenforced message or DB-state clause

lessons.key: surviving_mutant::when a query result is filtered on a column an index also sorts by prove order by is load bearing with a test whose data filter can t be coincidentally satisfied by that index s own scan order
lessons.text: When a query result is filtered on a column an index also sorts by, prove ORDER BY is load-bearing with a test whose data/filter can't be coincidentally satisfied by that index's own scan order.

lessons.key: ac_gap::when a spec ac lists multiple invalid input variants e g out of range vs non integer write a discriminating test for each variant not just the ones that need new code
lessons.text: When a spec AC lists multiple invalid-input variants (e.g. out-of-range vs. non-integer), write a discriminating test for each variant, not just the ones that need new code.

lessons.key: ac_gap::when a spec s own independent test names a specific input combination write that exact test rather than substituting a simpler case that exercises the same code path but not the same scenario
lessons.text: When a spec's own Independent Test names a specific input combination, write that exact test rather than substituting a simpler case that exercises the same code path but not the same scenario.

lessons.key: ac_gap::when a spec ac requires an error to be logged assert the log via caplog not just the response status body
lessons.text: When a spec AC requires an error to be logged, assert the log via caplog, not just the response status/body.

lessons.key: spec_precision_gap::when a spec ac is a conjunction of conditions write one test asserting the full conjunction rather than proving each condition in a separate test that individually omits the others
lessons.text: When a spec AC is a conjunction of conditions, write one test asserting the full conjunction rather than proving each condition in a separate test that individually omits the others.

lessons.key: surviving_mutant::add a test at the exact boundary value of every numeric ceiling comparison e g retry max retry not just values comfortably past it so a mutation is caught
lessons.text: Add a test at the exact boundary value of every numeric ceiling comparison (e.g. retry == MAX_RETRY), not just values comfortably past it, so a > -> >= mutation is caught

lessons.key: ac_gap::when an acceptance criterion requires both a positive outcome and a negative side effect claim e g no republish no failure log entry assert both explicitly not just the positive outcome
lessons.text: When an acceptance criterion requires both a positive outcome and a negative side-effect claim (e.g. no republish, no failure-log entry), assert both explicitly, not just the positive outcome
